name: Devil's food cake
origin: An early-20th-century American dark chocolate cake, named as the rich, dark counterpart to angel food; built on the American 'high-ratio' method (sugar mass exceeding flour mass, held in emulsion by a generous fat) that Gisslen documents as the industrial standard for moist, tender chocolate layer cakes.

ingredients.note: residual fat fraction of 20% (of flour mass) cocoa powder, split by this registry's own cocoa-powder substance record (packages/data/substances/cocoa-powder.json: 137 g residual press fat per kg, the rest non-fat solids)
non-fat solids fraction of the same 20%-of-flour cocoa powder line above
buttermilk's mild lactic acid, together with the cocoa's own acidity, is what the bicarbonate below actually reacts against

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: add eggs and cocoa
process.description: beat in eggs, then the sifted cocoa powder

process.name: alternate flour and buttermilk
process.description: fold in the flour (with bicarbonate and salt) and buttermilk in alternating additions, starting and ending with flour

notes: Sugar above flour mass (130%) with buttermilk carrying most of the hydration is the real signature of the American high-ratio chocolate cake method (Gisslen, Professional Baking). Cocoa powder's fat content (USDA FoodData Central, unsweetened cocoa powder: ~21 g fat per 100 g) is split into its own fat-role line so the formulation's real fat mass includes cocoa butter, not just the added butter.
